results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, and let $U$ and $V$ be the Lucas sequences $U(P, Q)$ and $V(P, Q)$. Then $U_{2n} = U_n V_n$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Divisibility of Lucas sequences at divisible indices

results.title: Lucas sequences under negation of the first parameter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For integers $P$ and $Q \ne 0$ and every natural number $n$, the Lucas sequences $U$ and $V$ satisfy $U_n(-P, Q) = (-1)^{n+1} U_n(P, Q)$ and $V_n(-P, Q) = (-1)^n V_n(P, Q)$.

results.title: Shift congruence for the Lucas recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U = U(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \ne 0$, and let $(W_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers with $W_{n+2} = P W_{n+1} - Q W_n$ for every $n \ge 0$. If $t \ge 0$ and $m$ are integers with $m \mid U_t$ and $\gcd(m, Q) = 1$, then $W_{n+t} \equiv U_{t+1} W_n \pmod{m}$ for every $n \ge 0$.

results.title: When $p^{i+1}$ divides $U_{2n}$, for a prime power $p^i$ exactly dividing $P$

results.title: Rank of appearance in a Lucas sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U = U(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \ne 0$. The rank of appearance $\rho(m)$ of a natural number $m$ in $U$ is the least positive integer $r$ with $m \mid U_r$; when no positive $r$ has $m \mid U_r$, $\rho(m) = 0$.

results.title: Rank of appearance is at most any positive index of divisibility

results.title: Index of the Lucas pseudoprime congruences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P, Q$ be integers with $Q \neq 0$ and $D = P^2 - 4Q$. For a natural number $N$, the index is $N - (D/N)$, where $(D/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol, replaced by $0$ when this difference is negative. For $N > 1$ the difference is positive.

results.title: Lucas pseudoprimes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P, Q$ be integers with $Q \neq 0$, let $U_n$ be the Lucas sequence of $(P, Q)$ and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. A natural number $N$ is a Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P, Q$ if $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$ and $N$ divides $U_{N - (D/N)}$, where $(D/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol.

results.title: Lucas pseudoprimes of the second kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P, Q$ be integers with $Q \neq 0$, let $U_n$ be the Lucas sequence of $(P, Q)$ and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. A natural number $N$ is a Lucas pseudoprime of the second kind with parameters $P, Q$ if $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$ and $U_N \equiv (D/N) \pmod{N}$, where $(D/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol.

results.title: Dickson pseudoprimes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ and $Q \ne 0$ be integers with discriminant $D = P^2 - 4Q$, and let $(V_n)$ be the companion Lucas sequence $V(P, Q)$. A natural number $N$ is a Dickson pseudoprime with parameters $P$ and $Q$ if $N$ is odd, $N > 1$, $N$ is not prime, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and $V_N \equiv P \pmod N$.

results.title: Dickson pseudoprimes of the second kind
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Euler pseudoprime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a$ be an integer. A natural number $N$ is an Euler pseudoprime to the base $a$ when $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(a, N) = 1$, and $a^{(N-1)/2} \equiv (a/N) \pmod N$, where $(a/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol.

results.title: Euler–Lucas pseudoprime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U$ and $V$ be the Lucas sequences with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \neq 0$, and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. A natural number $N$ is an Euler–Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P, Q$ when $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and, writing $\varepsilon = (D/N)$ for the Jacobi symbol, $N \mid U_{(N-\varepsilon)/2}$ if the Jacobi symbol $(Q/N)$ equals $1$, and $N \mid V_{(N-\varepsilon)/2}$ if $(Q/N) = -1$.

results.title: Strong Lucas pseudoprimes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P, Q$ be integers with $Q \neq 0$, let $U_n$ and $V_n$ be the Lucas sequences of $(P, Q)$ and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. A natural number $N$ is a strong Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P, Q$ if $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and, writing $N - (D/N) = 2^s d$ with $d$ odd, where $(D/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol, either $N \mid U_d$ or $N \mid V_{2^r d}$ for some $r$ with $0 \le r < s$.

results.title: Super pseudoprime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P, Q$ be integers with $Q \neq 0$, let $D = P^2 - 4Q$, and let $S$ be a property of natural numbers. A natural number $N$ is a super pseudoprime of type $S$ with parameters $(P, Q)$ when $N$ is odd, $N > 1$, $N$ is not prime, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and every divisor $d > 1$ of $N$ is prime or has property $S$.

results.title: Carmichael's primitive divisor theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be coprime integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair with discriminant $D = P^2 - 4Q > 0$, and let $(U_n)$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. Then for every $n \ge 1$ with $n \notin \{1, 2, 6, 12\}$, the term $U_n$ has a primitive prime divisor: a prime $p$ that divides $U_n$ but divides no $U_s$ with $1 \le s < n$.

results.title: Weighted binary digit sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the weighted binary digit sum of $n$ is $a(n) = \sum_i i \cdot 2^i$, where $i$ runs over the indices of the $1$ bits in the binary expansion of $n$. Equivalently, if $n = 2^{a_1} + \dots + 2^{a_t}$ with distinct exponents $a_1, \dots, a_t$, then $a(n) = a_1 2^{a_1} + \dots + a_t 2^{a_t}$; in particular $a(0) = 0$.

results.title: Lebesgue differentiation along shrinking off-center intervals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a locally integrable `f : ℝ → ℝ`, for almost every `u`, the averages of `f` over intervals `[a n, b n]` converge to `f u` whenever the lengths `b n - a n > 0` tend to `0` and the distance from `u` to the midpoint of `[a n, b n]` is at most twice the length.

results.title: Progressive processes are jointly measurable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A progressive process is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` (reading `u : ℝ` through `Real.toNNReal`).

results.title: Truncation of a progressive process is progressive

results.title: Measurability of time averages of a progressive process
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Delayed-average approximation of a progressive process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The delayed-average approximation of a progressive process `H` on `[0, t]`, truncated at level `M`, with `n + 1` intervals: on `(t_k, t_{k+1}]`, with `t_k = k t / (n + 1)`, it equals the average of `truncation (H ·) M` over `[t_{k-1}, t_k]` for `k ≥ 1`, and `0` for `k = 0`. For `M ≤ 0` the truncation, and hence the approximation, is `0`.

results.title: Convergence of the delayed averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a progressive `H` and a finite measure `P`, the delayed-average approximations of the truncation of `H` at level `M` converge to it in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω` as the mesh `t / (n + 1)` tends to `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, proof of Lemma 3.2.4(b)).

results.title: Sets given by consecutive differences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $a$ and natural numbers $g_1, \dots, g_r$, the set $(a \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$ is the finite set of integers $\{a, a + g_1, a + g_1 + g_2, \dots, a + g_1 + \dots + g_r\}$; for $r = 0$ it is $\{a\}$.

results.title: Prepending a gap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integer $a$ and natural numbers $g_1, \dots, g_r$ ($r \ge 0$), write $(a \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$ for the set of partial sums $\{a, a + g_1, \dots, a + g_1 + \dots + g_r\}$. Then for every natural number $g$, $(a \mid g, g_1, \dots, g_r) = \{a\} \cup (a + g \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$.

results.title: An example of difference notation

results.title: Strict preference order
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A strict total order on a type $\alpha$ is a binary relation $<$ on $\alpha$ that is irreflexive ($a < a$ holds for no $a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements ($a \ne b$ implies $a < b$ or $b < a$). In the Gale–Shapley development it models strict preference.

results.title: Building a strict total order from a relation
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A binary relation $<$ on a set $\alpha$ that is irreflexive ($a \not< a$ for all $a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements ($a \ne b$ implies $a < b$ or $b < a$) defines a strict total order on $\alpha$ whose relation is $<$.

results.title: Relation of a strict total order
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The relation of a strict total order $T$ on a set $\alpha$ is its underlying binary relation $\lt _T$ on $\alpha$, which is irreflexive, transitive, and relates any two distinct elements in one direction or the other.

results.title: Irreflexivity of a strict total order
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $T$ be a strict total order on a set $\alpha$, with relation $\lt _T$. Then $a \lt _T a$ fails for every $a \in \alpha$.

results.title: Transitivity of a strict total order
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $<$ be the relation of a strict total order on a type $\alpha$. If $a, b, c \in \alpha$ satisfy $a < b$ and $b < c$, then $a < c$.

results.title: Strict total orders are total on distinct elements
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $<$ be the relation of a strict total order on a type $\alpha$. If $a, b \in \alpha$ and $a \ne b$, then $a < b$ or $b < a$.

results.title: Strict total orders are determined by their relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be strict total orders on a set $\alpha$, with relations $\lt _T$ and $\lt _{T'}$. If $x \lt _T y \iff x \lt _{T'} y$ for all $x, y \in \alpha$, then $T = T'$.

results.title: Men's preferences
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For sets $M$ (men) and $W$ (women), a preference profile of the men assigns to each $m \in M$ a strict total order on $W$, the preferences of $m$.

results.title: Women's preference profile
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For types $M$ and $W$, a preference profile of $W$ over $M$ assigns to each $w \in W$ a strict total order on $M$, read as the strict preference of $w$ among the elements of $M$.

results.title: Perfect matching
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A perfect matching between sets $M$ and $W$ is a bijection $\mu \colon M \to W$, which matches each $m \in M$ with $\mu(m) \in W$.

results.title: Blocking pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be sets. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order $\lt _m$ of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order $\lt _w$ of preference on $M$, where $x \lt _m y$ means that $m$ prefers $x$ to $y$, and likewise for $\lt _w$. For a perfect matching $\mu$ between $M$ and $W$, a pair $(m, w) \in M \times W$ is a blocking pair when $w \lt _m \mu(m)$ and $m \lt _w \mu^{-1}(w)$,…

results.title: Stable perfect matching
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be sets. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. A perfect matching $\mu$ between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences when no pair $(m, w) \in M \times W$ is a blocking pair for $\mu$.

results.title: Existence of stable perfect matchings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be finite sets with the same number of elements. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. Then some perfect matching between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences.

results.title: Gale–Shapley theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $W$ be finite sets with the same number of elements. Suppose that each $m \in M$ has a strict total order of preference on $W$ and each $w \in W$ has a strict total order of preference on $M$. Then some perfect matching between $M$ and $W$ is stable for these preferences.

results.title: Preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, number $n$ men and $n$ women by $0, \dots, n - 1$. A preference profile $P = (M, W)$ for them consists of a permutation $M_i$ of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ for each man $i$ and a permutation $W_j$ of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ for each woman $j$: $M_i(r)$ is the woman man $i$ ranks at zero-based position $r$, and $W_j(r)$ is the man woman $j$ ranks at position $r$.

results.title: Rank of a woman for a man
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, the rank of woman $j$ for man $i$ is the zero-based position $r \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ at which $i$ ranks $j$, so his favorite has rank $0$ and his least favorite has rank $n - 1$.

results.title: A woman's rank of a man
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women, the rank that woman $j$ gives man $i$ is the zero-based position at which she ranks him, that is, the paper's ranking minus one.

results.title: Soulmate pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, man $i$ and woman $j$ are soulmates when each ranks the other first: $j$ is the first choice of $i$ and $i$ is the first choice of $j$.

results.title: Number of soulmate pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of soulmate pairs of a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women is the number of pairs $(i, j)$ of a man $i$ and a woman $j$ that are soulmates in $P$, that is, each ranks the other first.

results.title: Men's preferences induced by rankings
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, each man $i$ gets the strict total order on the women in which $i$ prefers woman $a$ to woman $b$ exactly when he ranks $a$ at an earlier position than $b$.

results.title: Women's preference orders of a profile
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women, each woman $j$ gets the strict total order on the men in which man $a$ comes before (is preferred to) man $b$ exactly when woman $j$ ranks $a$ at an earlier position than $b$.

results.title: Stable matching
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, a matching $\mu$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$, is stable when no man and woman both strictly prefer each other to their own spouses. Equivalently, $\mu$ is a stable perfect matching for the strict preferences induced by the men's and the women's rankings.

results.title: Stability in terms of ranks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, a matching $\mu$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$, is stable if and only if there are no man $i$ and woman $j$ such that $i$ ranks $j$ strictly above his wife $\mu(i)$ and $j$ ranks $i$ strictly above her husband $\mu^{-1}(j)$.

results.title: Hell-couple
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, and let $\mu$ be a matching in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$. Man $i$ and his wife $\mu(i)$ form a hell-couple when each ranks the other last: $i$ ranks $\mu(i)$ in his last position and $\mu(i)$ ranks $i$ in her last position.

results.title: Number of Latin squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $L_n$ is the number of Latin squares of order $n$: families $(M_0, \dots, M_{n-1})$ of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the rows) such that for every position $r$ the entries $M_0(r), \dots, M_{n-1}(r)$ (column $r$) are pairwise distinct.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women. The number $p_t(i)$ of women man $i$ has proposed to after $t$ rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ is defined by $p_0(i) = 0$ and, for every $t$, $p_{t+1}(i) = p_t(i)$ if man $i$ is provisionally engaged in the state $p_t$ and $p_{t+1}(i) = p_t(i) + 1$ otherwise: in each round every man who is not provisionally engaged proposes to his…

results.title: Number of Gale–Shapley rounds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a preference profile $P$ for $n$ men and $n$ women, the number of rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ is the least $t$ such that every man is provisionally engaged after $t$ rounds (or $0$ if there is no such $t$).

results.title: No proposals before the first round
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every preference profile, after zero rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm every man has made zero proposals.

results.title: One round of the Gale–Shapley algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women and let $t$ be a natural number. After $t + 1$ rounds of the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$, a man who is provisionally engaged after $t$ rounds has made as many proposals as after $t$ rounds, and every other man has made one proposal more than after $t$ rounds.

results.title: Gale–Shapley rounds with no participants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the preference profile with no men and no women, the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm takes zero rounds.

results.title: A profile has at most $n$ soulmate pairs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women has at most $n$ soulmate pairs, since a man's soulmate is his first choice.

results.title: Latin squares of order zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is exactly one Latin square of order $0$, that is, $L_0 = 1$.

results.title: Gale–Shapley rounds when all men have the same preferences
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women in which all men rank the women in the same order. Then the men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ ends in exactly $n$ rounds.

results.title: When the Gale–Shapley algorithm ends in one round
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women. The men-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm on $P$ ends in exactly one round if and only if every woman is the first choice of exactly one man.

results.title: Counting disjoint preference profiles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women disjoint if for every pair of positions $(r, s)$ there is exactly one man–woman pair in which the man ranks the woman at position $r$ and the woman ranks the man at position $s$. For every natural number $n$, the number of disjoint profiles is at most $(n^2)!$ and is divisible by $(n!)^2$.

results.title: At most one hell-couple in a stable matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile of $n$ men and $n$ women, and let $\mu$ be a stable matching for $P$, in which man $i$ marries woman $\mu(i)$. Then at most one man $i$ forms a hell-couple with his wife $\mu(i)$.

results.title: A hell-couple belongs to every stable matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be stable matchings for $P$. If man $i$ and his wife $\mu(i)$ form a hell-couple in $\mu$ (each ranks the other last), then $\nu(i) = \mu(i)$.

results.title: Profiles with a pair of outcasts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a preference profile for $n$ men and $n$ women, a man $i$ and a woman $j$ form a pair of outcasts when every man other than $i$ ranks $j$ last and every woman other than $j$ ranks $i$ last. The number of preference profiles with at least one pair of outcasts is $14$ if $n = 2$ and $n^4 ((n-1)!)^{2n}$ if $n \ne 2$ (this is $0$ for $n = 0$).

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a letter $a$ of an alphabet, a word $w$ belongs to the Kleene star of the language $\{a\}$ whose only word is the one-letter word $a$ if and only if $w = a^k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Radix trie
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For types $\alpha$ and $\beta$, a radix trie with keys that are lists over $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is a node made of an optional value in $\beta$ and a finite list of child edges, each a pair of a label, which is a list over $\alpha$, and a radix trie (the subtree at the end of the edge).

results.title: Empty radix trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The empty radix trie is the single node that stores no value and has no child edges; it contains no key-value entries.

results.title: Longest common prefix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is defined by recursion: it is empty if $s$ or $t$ is empty; if $s$ has first element $a$ and rest $s'$, and $t$ has first element $b$ and rest $t'$, it is $a$ followed by the longest common prefix of $s'$ and $t'$ when $a = b$, and empty when $a \ne b$.

results.title: Longest common prefix of a list with itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $s$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $s$ and $s$ is $s$.

results.title: A shared prefix factors out of the longest common prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $uv$ for the list $u$ followed by the list $v$. For lists $p$, $s$ and $t$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $ps$ and $pt$ is $p$ followed by the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$.

results.title: Characterization of the longest common prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, with longest common prefix $p$. Then there are lists $s'$ and $t'$ such that $s$ is $p$ followed by $s'$, $t$ is $p$ followed by $t'$, and either $s'$ is empty, or $t'$ is empty, or $s'$ and $t'$ are both nonempty with different first elements.

results.title: A list is its common prefix with another list followed by the rest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, and let $p$ be the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$. Then $s$ is $p$ followed by the list obtained by dropping the first $|p|$ elements of $s$, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$.

results.title: Longest common prefix in terms of dropped remainders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, let $p$ be their longest common prefix, of length $n$, and let $s'$ and $t'$ be the lists obtained from $s$ and $t$ by dropping their first $n$ elements. Then $s$ is $p$ followed by $s'$, $t$ is $p$ followed by $t'$, and either $s'$ is empty, or $t'$ is empty, or $s'$ and $t'$ are both nonempty with different first elements.

results.title: When the common prefix is the second list, the first list extends it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality. If the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is $t$, then $s$ is $t$ followed by the list obtained by dropping the first $|t|$ elements of $s$, where $|t|$ is the length of $t$.

results.title: The longest common prefix of a list and its prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$, $t$ and $u$ be lists over a type with decidable equality. If $s$ is $t$ followed by $u$, then the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is $t$.

results.title: Edge search by first symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a symbol $c$ and a list of edges, each a pair of a label (a list of symbols) and a subtree, this returns the first edge in the list whose label starts with $c$, or nothing if no label starts with $c$.

results.title: Replacing the child edge for a symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a symbol $c$, an edge $e$ (a pair of a label and a radix trie) and a list of child edges, this operation replaces the first edge of the list whose label starts with $c$ by $e$ and keeps all other edges in order. If no label in the list starts with $c$, it appends $e$ at the end of the list.

results.summary: For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty radix trie returns no value.

results.title: Lookup of a key just inserted into a radix trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every radix trie $T$, key $k$ and value $v$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $T$ by inserting $v$ at $k$ returns $v$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every radix trie $T$, all keys $k \ne k'$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $T$ by inserting $v$ at $k'$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T$.

results.title: Path-compressed root
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A radix trie is path-compressed at its root when its root node stores a value or has at least two child edges.

results.title: Valid radix trie
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Validity of radix tries is defined inductively: a node is valid when every label of its child edges is nonempty, the first symbols of the labels of its child edges are pairwise distinct, and for each child edge the subtree at its end is valid and path-compressed at its root (its root stores a value or has at least two child edges).

results.title: The empty radix trie is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all types $\alpha$ and $\beta$, the empty radix trie whose keys are lists over $\alpha$ and whose values lie in $\beta$ is valid.

results.title: Sibling edge labels start with distinct symbols

results.title: Hamiltonian agrees with Physlib's Ising energy
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The Hamiltonian `hamiltonian G h` is Physlib's Ising energy `CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy` of the model with coupling `J = 1` and field `h`, on the region of all vertices.

results.title: Ising model as a Physlib canonical ensemble
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ising model on a finite graph `G` with field `h`, as Physlib's finite canonical ensemble: microstates are spin configurations, the energy is `hamiltonian G h`, and the measure is the counting measure.

results.title: Ising partition function agrees with Physlib's partition function

results.title: Ising Gibbs probability agrees with Physlib's canonical probability
